entries.title: Scalar optimal values, attainment, and unboundedness
entries.reproduction_basis: For x>0, compare 1/x, -log(x), and x log(x). The first tends to zero as x tends to infinity and remains positive, so the infimum is not attained. The second decreases without bound. The last has derivative 1+log(x) and positive second derivative 1/x, so its unique minimum is x=1/e, with value -1/e. A bounded scalar optimizer independently checks this last value.

entries.title: Minimal matrix upper bounds via weighted SDP
entries.reproduction_basis: For three explicitly published new positive-definite 2-by-2 matrices, solve min tr(WX) subject to X−Aᵢ positive semidefinite. Use two positive-definite weights, I and diag(4,1), to obtain different minimal upper bounds. The dual matrices sum to W and their weighted traces give an independent lower bound; stationarity and primal-dual gaps certify both results. Since W is positive definite, a strictly smaller feasible matrix in the PSD order would strictly improve the objective, proving minimality.

This new instance demonstrates the same weighted-SDP minimal-upper-bound construction. Positive-definite W ensures no strictly smaller PSD-feasible upper bound can dominate the computed solution.

entries.title: Huber regression with two outliers
entries.reproduction_basis: Fit y≈α+βt to the 42 published points. Least squares minimizes the sum of squared residuals. The robust fit minimizes the sum of Huber losses with threshold M=1: r² for |r|≤1 and 2|r|−1 otherwise. The second expression is continuous at the threshold; the comment in the old companion code omits its constant but its QP implements the correct loss. Compare the convex solve against an independent analytic-gradient minimization and check the normal equations.

entries.reproduction_basis: Write H=A^T A and g=A^T b. On each sphere ||x||²=α, diagonalizing H reduces stationarity to a scalar secular equation in a Lagrange multiplier. Its root on the positive-semidefinite branch gives the minimum; the corresponding negative-definite branch gives the maximum. Both boundaries of the achievable set are computed. Independent two-variable semidefinite duals certify all nonzero-radius extrema. The lower-left boundary through the zero and least-squares endpoints is the Pareto frontier.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_basic.py fig_4_11; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

independent_checks.name: all secular extrema versus SDP dual bounds

entries.title: Four-asset portfolio risk-return trade-off
entries.reproduction_basis: For each μ>0 solve min (μ/2)w^TΣw−r^Tw, subject to w≥0 and 1^Tw=1. The covariance and expected returns are the printed four-asset constants. Include the two limiting portfolios explicitly. Plot return against standard deviation and stacked allocations. Independent constrained SciPy optimization checks every QP objective. The factor 1/2 follows the companion QP convention and changes only the parameterization of the frontier.

entries.title: Nonconvex scalar primal and Lagrangian dual numerical illustration
entries.reproduction_basis: The original plotted functions are unavailable, so use two explicitly new nonconvex quartics: f₀(x)=(x²−1)²+0.2x and f₁(x)=(x²−0.46²)(x²+0.1). The feasible interval is[−0.46,0.46]; direct derivative analysis and endpoint comparison locate the primal optimum. For every nonnegative multiplier, the Lagrangian remains coercive quartic, so enumerating all real roots of its cubic derivative obtains the global infimum. Plot the objective, constraint, ten Lagrangians and concave dual; verify stationary roots, weak duality and discrete concavity. The new objective value is deliberately distinguished from the book’s1.54.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_signals.py fig_5_1_5_2; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

notes: The original formulas for Figures5.1–5.2 were not published or located in official companion sources. Both functions here are newly specified nonconvex quartics. Their feasible interval is[-0.46,0.46], but the new objective value is not the book’s1.54. All ten Lagrangian curves and the concave dual function belong to this explicitly different instance.

entries.title: Total-variation signal reconstruction
entries.reproduction_basis: Generate the source’s2000-point piecewise signal and new standard-deviation0.1 noise. Compute the100-point quadratic-smoothing trade-off and three comparison reconstructions. Solve fifteen TV problems min(1/2)||x−y||²+λ||Dx||₁; separately solve the book’s exact variation budgets10,8,5 as constrained QPs. The source15-point sweep and its nearest-grid comparisons remain separately recorded. Dual box-constrained difference variables provide feasible lower bounds and stationarity certificates. Report both absolute and normalized primal-dual gaps, with relative acceptance1e−6, avoiding misleading absolute tolerances across widely different objective scales.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_signals.py fig_6_11; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

entries.title: Comparing four residual penalties
entries.reproduction_basis: On a new100-by-30 PCG64 instance, minimize four residual losses: absolute, squared, deadzone max(|r|−0.5,0), and logarithmic −log(1−r²). Scale the shared response so x=0 is strictly in the barrier domain. Compare four residual histograms. Independent HiGHS LPs check the piecewise-linear losses; normal equations check least squares; analytic-gradient BFGS checks the barrier objective. The old CVXOPT least-squares branch accidentally solves with a zero right-hand side; this implementation solves the actual stated A x+b problem.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_signals.py fig_6_2; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

notes: New PCG64 seed602 100-by-30 instance. Common b is scaled by 1/(1.1 max|b|), making x=0 strictly feasible for the logarithmic loss. This follows the CVXOPT input convention; its source explicitly says its own data differ from the book. Unlike the old CVXOPT least-squares branch, the right-hand side is actually -b rather than a zero vector.

entries.title: Gabor basis pursuit and time-frequency recovery
entries.reproduction_basis: Build the full501-by-30561 Gabor dictionary and minimize ||Ax−y||²+||x||₁. An active-column strategy is only a computational device: every iteration computes all30561 dual correlations, and termination requires a valid full-dictionary primal-dual gap. Refit least squares on coefficients exceeding1e−5 and report count and relative squared error. Execute the CVX endpoint grid with0.001 tail truncation, CVXOPT k/501 untruncated grid, and the book’s literal0.005k grid ending at2.5. Plot dictionary examples, signals, residuals and selected time-frequency atoms separately for all three conventions.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_basis.py fig_6_21; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

notes: The text says501 equally spaced samples on[0,1], but prints0.005k, whose endpoint is2.5. CVX usesk/500 and removes Gaussian tails below0.001. CVXOPT usesk/501 without truncation. All three conventions are executed and reported separately.

The full dictionary has30561 columns. Active-column optimization is accepted only after a full-dictionary dual certificate; this is not a reduced-dictionary substitute. The l1 optimum is followed by least-squares refitting on coefficients exceeding1e-5, matching the source workflow.

The book reports42 selected atoms and relative squared error2.6e-4. Those are comparison benchmarks; source ambiguities and solver-sensitive support thresholds preclude silently asserting that every convention must recover them.

entries.title: Chebyshev bounds for symbol detection
entries.reproduction_basis: Use the six published Voronoi vertices to recover all seven constellation symbols. For each of the first three symbols and151 noise levels, minimize E[q(X)] over nonnegative quadratic majorants of the outside-cell indicator. Semidefinite constraints implement the halfspace S-lemma. The lower detection bound is1−E[q(X)]. At unit variance, dual PSD matrices recover an extremal atomic distribution; its total mass, zero mean and identity covariance are checked independently. Plot the constellation, atoms, quadratic level set and all three bound curves.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_probability.py fig_7_5; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

notes: Extremal outside atoms can lie exactly on Voronoi boundaries. The strict/open-cell worst-case probability is the limiting distribution under arbitrarily small outward perturbations; a tie-breaking convention should not be mistaken for a discrepancy in the moment bound.

entries.title: Chernoff and Monte Carlo detection bounds
entries.reproduction_basis: Project the origin onto each competing Voronoi region. If its squared distance is dᵢ², the Gaussian Chernoff union bound gives detection probability at least1−Σexp(−dᵢ²/(2σ²)). Independently verify all six projection QPs with SciPy. Run100000 new standard-Gaussian draws across201 noise levels, using common random numbers; display pointwise95% Wilson intervals. Independent one-dimensional Gaussian quadrature at eleven noise levels checks the simulation and verifies the deterministic bounds.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_probability.py fig_7_8; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

entries.title: D-, E- and A-optimal experiment design
entries.reproduction_basis: For the 20 published candidate vectors form information M=Σw_i v_i v_i^T on the simplex. D design maximizes log det M, E design maximizes its smallest eigenvalue, and A design minimizes tr(M⁻¹). Independent constrained SciPy objectives check all three solutions. The relevant dual quadratic forms give enclosing ellipsoids; direct containment inequalities are verified. Covariance M⁻¹ yields the 90% Gaussian confidence ellipsoids using the two-dimensional χ² quantile, compared with uniform allocation.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_statistics.py fig_7_9; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

entries.title: Approximate linear classification comparison
entries.reproduction_basis: Compare sum of hinge slacks, ||a||₂+0.1 times hinge slacks, and logistic negative log-likelihood on the same two published fifty-point classes. The margin is yᵢ(aᵀxᵢ−b). Independent dual optimization verifies both hinge classifiers; the logistic gradient certifies its optimum. Misclassifications have negative margin and correctly classified points strictly inside the slab have margin in (0,1), excluding a 1e−6 boundary tolerance. The verified companion result has fourteen such SVM points, while the book caption says fifteen; this discrepancy is explicit and prevents an exact-output-match claim.

verification.test_command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python examples/application_geometry.py fig_8_10; python -m pytest tests/test_worked_applications.py -q

entries.reproduction_basis: Generate the source’s 100/120 initial radial points and exchanged wedge using new seed0. For each degree one through four, construct all bivariate monomials and solve the signed-margin feasibility LP. Degree-three infeasibility is independently certified by nonnegative weights summing to one whose weighted signed feature rows sum to zero, a Farkas witness. Degree four admits a separator; minimize its coefficient norm to select a stable witness and plot its zero contour. The seed selection and unsuccessful first trial are disclosed.

entries.title: Minimum-volume enclosing and maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoids
entries.reproduction_basis: The enclosing ellipse is {x:||Ax+b||₂≤1}; minimize −log det A with each polygon vertex inside. For the inscribed ellipse {c+Bu:||u||₂≤1}, maximize log det B subject to aᵢᵀc+||Baᵢ||₂≤bᵢ. The same six published vertices define both problems. Independently check the explicit matrix KKT stationarity conditions using returned conic multipliers. Also verify both factor-two containment statements directly: half the enclosing ellipse is inside the polygon, and twice the inscribed ellipse contains every vertex.

Plot the three centers, barrier contours and the local Hessian ellipse. LP duality and all center feasibility conditions are checked.
